CA lemon law has always been consumer friendly (e.g. consumer is entitled to attorney fees in they “prevail”, but not the other way around; availability of civil penalties of up to two times actual damages for “wilful failure” to comply with lemon law), but the recent massive year to year increase of lemon law lawsuit filings is a result of a much more aggressive LL consumer attorney bar. They are not only filing more cases but are also adding additional claims like fraud and unfair business practices that holds up resolution of the case (essentially holding the statutorily defined LL claims and its damages hostage because of the availability of punitive damages. 
Additionally, recent appellate law in the area is mostly plaintiff friendly is very impactful. For example, a recent CA Supreme Court cases found that auto manufacturers are not entitled to a monetary set off if the plaintiff sells/trades in their vehicle or receives receives insurance proceeds for an accident. This means that a plaintiff, either before or after filing a lawsuit, can sell their vehicle and still receive full restitution for their vehicle, allowing for double recovery. 
Because the deck is so stacked against the auto companies, you see a lot more repurchase (or more) offers early in cases in an attempt to keep attorney fees down. It also means a lot more cases go to trial, because auto companies offer high statutory settlement offers and if plaintiff fails to beat the offer at trial, then attorney fees are cutoff and the auto company is entitled to some costs. I’ve had 2 jury trials in last 3 months and probably will have 2-3 more this year at a minimum. That’s quite a lot considering 99% of civil cases settle before trial.

Proposals:
Draft Lottery: Implement a draft lottery to reduce the incentive to tank.
Performance Penalties: Penalize teams with a significant gap between potential points and actual points scored.
Consolation Tournament Incentives: Offer prizes or incentives for the consolation tournament to keep teams competitive.
Context: Significant concern over tanking's impact on league integrity and competitiveness. Implementing these measures aims to ensure fair play and maintain interest throughout the season.

Proposals:
Caddy Punishment: Last place finisher acts as a caddy during a league golf trip.
Car Decoration: Sacko must place a specific item on their car for a year.
Beer Mile: Sacko must complete a beer mile (chug a beer, run a lap, repeated four times).
Trophy Duty: Sacko is responsible for ordering and engraving the league trophy.
Concert Attendance: Sacko must attend a concert alone, chosen by the champion, and film themselves during the first song and encore.
IKEA Desk Assembly: Sacko must livestream themselves assembling an IKEA desk. If not completed in the allotted time, the champion gets to change the Sacko's team name for the following year.
Sacko Shirt: Sacko must wear a "Sacko" shirt for 11 regular season weeks, dedicating a drink, joint, or meal to another team each week and posting it on social media. Designs for the shirt to be voted on at the owner's meeting.

Early Trade Deadline: Maintain or move the trade deadline earlier in the season to force strategic decisions sooner.
Later Trade Deadline: Move the trade deadline closer to the playoffs for more flexibility.

Context: Ongoing debates about the timing of the trade deadline and ensuring fairness in trades.

Proposal: Invest league dues in high-yield CDs or money market accounts to earn interest on the funds.
